But there’s something heartening about those new things settling into age, like a fecund garden becoming slightly unwieldy, or a pair of shoes getting more comfortable as you use them. Similarly, I’ve always enjoyed the way a well-made leather case ages as it weathers the trials and tribulations of everyday life. Traditionally called a patina, it’s the lived-in quality that a piece of leather inherits as it absorbs skin oils, scratches, and the unpredictability of weather. more…

items.title: You Can Now Try Apple's Unreleased Copland OS in Your Browser
items.snippet: In the mid–1990s, Apple worked on an operating system called Copland, which was announced but never commercially released because of project management issues and feature creep. Parts of Copland were eventually included in Mac OS 7.6 and Mac OS 8, but it was so problematic as a whole that Apple nixed it before it was finished. Michael Steil, who works to reverse engineer vintage hardware and software, was recently able to get Copland running in emulation. He modified the open-source Power Mac emulator DingusPPC, and he said it took 11 patches to get Copland up and running. items.title: Nvidia CEO says 'we have to shut the labs down' if AI experiments are unsafe
items.snippet: In a recent interview, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that if frontier labs have unsafe models, they should shut the labs down, calling the current calls for regulation a "distraction."

items.title: The three-pronged future of custom PC building — from repurposing forgotten parts to ultra-premium works of gaming art
items.snippet: This is probably the worst time ever for PC building. Here’s how and why I think the hobby (and the market) still have a future to look forward to.

items.title: Leading semiconductor analyst says AMD should be investigated for 'treason' over availability of restricted chips in China
items.snippet: Top semiconductor analysis firm accuses AMD of treason, AMD says it could have been 'diversion' of an export-controlled adaptable radio platform.

items.title: GMKtec Evo-X3 review: Strix Halo in a brand new suit
items.snippet: GMKtec has radically remodeled its AMD Strix Halo flagship AI mini PC. The statuesque redesign looks more premium and stays cool and quiet, but the Evo-X3 is around twice the price of the Evo-X2, with the same chip, which we reviewed back in February.

items.title: Save $149 on this 3-item gaming combo from Newegg
items.snippet: Fight back against the RAMpocolypse with this 3-item Newegg combo that features the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, 32GB Corsair Vengeance RAM, and Asus TUF X870E motherboard for only $1,050, a $149 savings

items.title: Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI
items.snippet: Micron is reportedly ending production of its 2GB GDDR7 chips, shifting attention toward higher-density 3GB parts used in more lucrative professional and AI-focused GPUs.

items.title: Lucky 3D artist scores Jensen Huang-signed RTX 5090 from used marketplace that's worth up to $15,000
items.snippet: A 3D artist looking to build a new workstation bought this RTX 5090 off of a used marketplace expecting a unit autographed by an Asus executive. But when they opened the box of the GPU, they were surprised to find that it was actually autographed by Jensen Huang himself.

items.title: New wireless Wi-Fi 7 external GPU box comes with a built-in 4TB SSD for local AI
items.snippet: WiCi wireless external GPU with onboard storage puts AI workloads reach of local machines via WiFi 7.

items.title: China’s ultimate gaming GPU hits a performance wall
items.snippet: The latest review of the Lisuan Tech LX 7G100 shows performance comparable to AMD's Radeon RX 580 but trails the GeForce RTX 2060.

items.title: Save big on this vivid 27-inch OLED monitor with fast 240Hz refresh rate
items.snippet: Get this MSI 27-inch 4K QD-OLED monitor for just $359. Enjoy vibrant colors, true blacks, a 240Hz refresh rate, and ultra-fast response time —perfect for gaming and productivity, and one of the best deals around for the specs

items.title: CyberPowerPC lands rare RTX 50-series Founders Edition cards in discounted Walmart rigs
items.snippet: CyberPowerPC is offering five different pre-built gaming PCs with either an RTX 5070, 5080, or 5090 Founders Edition GPUs paired with either an Intel or AMD X3D CPU. They also come with 32GB of DDR5 RAM and 1TB of NVMe SSD, all for reasonable prices.

items.title: Microsoft brings Snapdragon X2 Plus to 13-inch Surface Laptop, 12-inch Surface Pro
items.snippet: Microsoft's lowest-end systems are getting upgrades to Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon X2 Plus processors.

items.title: Alibaba claims new Qwen Image 2.1 AI model beats Google Nano Banana 2.0 with minuscule 7B parameter model
items.snippet: Alibaba Group's AI division has released Qwen 2.1 Image, an ultra-lightweight image generation model with just 7B parameters, able to run on local hardware like the RTX 3090.

items.title: $14,000 gaming PC features 70 handcrafted titanium cherry blossoms which unfurl as temperatures rise
items.snippet: The Aftershock PC Cherry Bloom includes 70 hand-crafted cherry blossoms made of titanium alloy that open and close with the heat generated by the PC.

items.title: Sony INZONE M10S II 27-inch 540 Hz QHD OLED gaming monitor review: A major player in a crowded field
items.snippet: Sony brings saturated color and speedy gameplay to the OLED genre with its INZONE M10S II 27-inch QHD monitor. It boasts a 540 Hz refresh rate, 720 Hz at HD resolution, Adaptive-Sync, HDR, and wide-gamut color.

items.title: China's ByteDance gained access to over 2,000 Nvidia B200 chips through Norway data center
items.snippet: UK-based Nscale signed a deal with Spring (SG) Pte Ltd, which is a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant ByteDance. The company did not make any direct mention of the TikTok parent in its filings for a U.S. IPO, while a supporting document only labeled Spring as a significant customer.

items.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China'
items.snippet: Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the M890’s performance with 216GB of memory as Alibaba targets 10T-parameter Qwen

items.title: Upgrade your gaming experience with this 27-inch Acer 1440p 270Hz panel that’s an incredible 45% off
items.snippet: Jump into high-refresh-rate 1440p gaming without breaking the bank: Acer's 27-inch 1440p 270Hz IPS gaming monitor is just $179, a whopping 45% off

items.title: AMD begins to add GDDR7 support to its Linux GPU drivers
items.snippet: Recent changes to AMD's Linux drivers to enable GDDR7 memory and other graphics IP blocks could indicate that that enablement work on its RDNA 5 GPUs is under way.

items.title: This 32GB Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 memory is the cheapest kit available
items.snippet: Get a great deal on 32GB Corsair Vengeance DDR5-6000 RAM. Just $439 after promo code SSF73844 yields one of the lowest priced 32GB kits available today

items.title: Durabook Z14I-DX3 rugged mobile workstation folds three screens into a 9.8 kg chassis
items.snippet: Built for military, emergency services and industrial applications, the Z14I-DX3 packs three sunlight-readable 14-inch touchscreens and up to RTX 5000 Ada graphics into one exceptionally rugged mobile workstation.

items.title: Get this spiffy, stealthy MSI Gaming Trio RTX 5090 for just $4,299
items.snippet: Walmart has MSI's GeForce RTX 5090 Gaming Trio for just $4299 as part of its GeForce Week event, a rare deal on the most powerful graphics card around as the AI boom drives prices ever higher.

items.title: ‘We’ll be the first to mine Bitcoin in space’ says Nvidia-backed startup
items.snippet: An Nvidia-backed startup plans to establish a Bitcoin mining operation in space before the year is out.

items.title: Gaming PC with RTX 5060, 32GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage gets $500 discount
items.snippet: Newegg's ABS Cyclone Aqua prebuilt combines Intel's 20-core Core i7-14700F with Nvidia's RTX 5060 8GB, and 32GB of DDR4 memory for less than the cost of building a comparable system

items.title: Microsoft adds pay-as-you-go pricing for extra OneDrive storage
items.snippet: Microsoft has added a “pay-as-you-go” option for OneDrive storage, providing an additional way for Microsoft 365 commercial customers to buy extra cloud storage capacity for users. Previously, increasing storage capacity for OneDrive users meant purchasing capacity “packs” for individual accounts, available in 100GB, 500GB, and 1TB through 6TB sizes. With the new consumption-based billing, Microsoft 365 admins can select which users’ accounts are eligible for additional capacity, with any usage above the licensed storage quota then automatically billed. The new billing option is currently in public preview for Microsoft 365 business customers, ahead of general availability starting November.

items.title: Similarweb and Chartbeat reveal how AI is starving media sites of search traffic
